digest.top_line: RTOG 1112: adding SBRT to sorafenib in locally advanced HCC gives mOS 15.8 vs 12.3mo, HR 0.77 (90% CI 0.59-1.01), 1-sided P=.06.
digest.tldr: Both items are RT-defining but neither settles its question. RTOG 1112 is the first randomised phase 3 of liver SBRT and misses its prespecified 1-sided OS test (P=.06) against a comparator (sorafenib) that IO-doublets have since displaced, though PFS is clean (HR 0.55). Head/neck reirradiation gets 31 consensus statements, with elective nodal irradiation rejected at 100% agreement.

sites.intro: Personalized 5-fraction SBRT (27.5-50 Gy, adapted to liver function) in a 74% macrovascular-invasion population: the PFS signal holds, the OS read is hostage to an obsolete systemic backbone.

studies.name: RTOG 1112
studies.tldr: mOS 15.8 vs 12.3mo, HR 0.77 (90% CI 0.59-1.01, 1-sided P=.06) adding SBRT to sorafenib in locally advanced HCC.
details: 🔍 Personalized SBRT 27.5-50 Gy in 5 fractions, dose adapted to liver function
🔍 Phase 3, 1:1, N=193 randomized / 177 eligible, accrual April 2013 to March 2021
🔍 Stratified by performance status, liver function, degree of metastases, macrovascular invasion
📊 Macrovascular invasion in 131/177 (74.0%), the population most likely to fail intrahepatically
⚠️ Primary OS endpoint not met on the prespecified 1-sided test (P=.06); the P=.04 is the adjusted analysis
⚠️ Accrual stopped early after SOC systemic therapy changed; sorafenib is no longer a first-line comparator
🔗 Comparator vintage is the core limitation: IMbrave150-era atezo/bev and durva/treme now define 1L, and SBRT was never tested against them
⚠️ QoL denominators are tiny (17 and 20 evaluable pts at 6mo); read as hypothesis-generating, not a QoL result
📊 Treatment-related deaths: 2 with sorafenib (1 liver failure), 1 with SBRT + sorafenib (lung infection)

verdict.rationale: Randomised phase 3, prespecified OS primary missed at P=.06 but PFS strongly positive and adjusted OS positive; comparator arm is now obsolete systemic therapy.
verdict.audience: Locally advanced HCC unsuitable/refractory to local-regional therapy, 74%…

studies.significance: The RT-attributable signal is PFS: HR 0.55 (0.40-0.75), a 3.7mo median gain, in a cohort 74% macrovascular-invasion positive where intrahepatic failure drives death. Personalized 27.5-50 Gy/5fx added no excess grade 3+ toxicity (47% vs 42%, P=.52), so the open decision is whether SBRT layers onto modern IO doublets, not whether it is deliverable.
studies.monday_clinic: In locally advanced HCC with macrovascular invasion unsuitable for local-regional therapy, this supports considering SBRT alongside first-line systemic therapy; it does not establish benefit added to current IO-based regimens, since the control arm was sorafenib.

primary_endpoint.name: Overall survival
primary_endpoint.stat_detail: HR 0.77 (90% CI 0.59-1.01), 1-sided P=.06, primary not met

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: Multicenter **phase 3 RCT**, 1:1, sorafenib vs SBRT followed by sorafenib. **193 randomized, 177 eligible**; accrual April 2013 to March 2021, **stopped early** when standard-of-care systemic therapy changed. Stratified by performance status, liver function, degree of metastases, macrovascular invasion.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: HCC **unsuitable for or refractory to standard local-regional therapies** and candidates for first-line systemic therapy. 150/177 (84.7%) male, median age 66 (IQR 60-72). **Macrovascular invasion in 131 (74.0%)**.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: **Personalized SBRT, 27.5 to 50 Gy in 5 fractions**, the dose individualized rather than fixed, then followed by sorafenib. No elective nodal or extrahepatic target volume reported in source.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: **Primary: overall survival.** Secondary: PFS, adverse events, quality of life. Data cutoff July 1, 2022.

analysis_sections.label: Safety
analysis_sections.body: Treatment-related grade 3+ AEs **39/83 (47%) with SBRT + sorafenib vs 37/88 (42%) with sorafenib, P=.52**. Treatment-related deaths: 2 sorafenib (death NOS, liver failure), 1 SBRT arm (lung infection). No excess hepatic toxicity signal reported in source.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents locally advanced HCC with macrovascular invasion that has exhausted or cannot receive local-regional therapy, entering first-line systemic treatment. Does not represent pts receiving contemporary IO-based first-line regimens, resectable or transplant-eligible disease, or Child-Pugh C liver function.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: The sorafenib control predates atezolizumab-bevacizumab and durvalumab-tremelimumab, so the absolute survival on both arms sits below modern 1L expectations and the SBRT increment is untested on an IO backbone. **Early accrual closure** left the trial underpowered for its own primary test, and QoL was assessed in only 17 and 20 evaluable pts at 6 months.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: A 3.5mo median OS gain with **HR 0.72 (0.52-0.99)** after adjustment, alongside a **PFS HR 0.55**, is the strongest randomised evidence to date that hepatic SBRT adds to systemic therapy in locally advanced HCC. The read is whether that increment survives the swap of sorafenib for an IO doublet, which no randomised trial has yet answered.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: PFS HR 0.55 (0.40-0.75) with personalized 27.5-50 Gy/5fx, no excess grade 3+ toxicity (47% vs 42%, P=.52), in a 74% macrovascular-invasion cohort. This is the randomised evidence that makes liver SBRT defensible at tumor board for pts exhausting local-regional options; the dose was individualized to liver function, so it transfers only with that planning discipline.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: The comparator is sorafenib, not an IO doublet, so this does not answer whether SBRT adds to atezolizumab-bevacizumab. What it does establish is that layering hepatic SBRT before systemic therapy cost nothing in grade 3+ toxicity (47% vs 42%, P=.52), which lowers the barrier to referring a macrovascular-invasion patient for RT while continuing planned systemic treatment.

Which macrovascular invasion subgroups derive the OS benefit?

sites.intro: Opinion, not outcome: the reirradiation statements that most change practice (RPA III eligibility, 66 Gy definitive dose, SBRT dose, cord/brainstem limits) are exactly the ones that stalled at moderate consensus.

studies.name: ReCOG/ESTRO/ASTRO HNSCC Reirradiation Consensus
studies.tldr: 31 statements, 24 (77%) at high consensus (≥85%); elective nodal irradiation not recommended, 100% agreement.
details: 🔍 Expert-driven clinical practice statement, single formal voting round, 17-panellist international ReCOG panel, fixed denominator (no opinion retained)
📐 Consensus thresholds prespecified: high ≥85%, moderate 70-84%, low <70%; evidence levels 1-4 adapted from Oxford CEBM

details.text: 📊 Statements reaching 100% agreement (evidence level in parentheses)
subdetails: Review previous plan to separate in-field recurrence from marginal failure (3)
No reirradiation for recurrence <6mo from previous RT, except urgent palliation (2)
Postoperative reirradiation for RPA class I with positive margins or ECE (2)
Elective nodal irradiation not recommended: no OS gain, more toxicity (3)
Carotid encasement >180° and previous ulceration elevate blowout risk (3)
Mandible ORN risk rises with cumulative EQD2 >114-119 Gy (3)

details.text: 📊 Dose corridors by technique / setting (consensus %, evidence level)
📊 Technique choice by RPA class and GTV volume (consensus %)

rows: SBRT with caution, severe toxicity risk

details.text: 📐 Cumulative OAR constraints, all in EQD2 (α/β 2 for late tissues)
subdetails: Spinal cord D0·1 cc ≤50 Gy, brainstem ≤55 Gy (70%, level 4)
Cord/brainstem surface ~60 Gy acceptable case-by-case (94%, level 4)
Recovery factors 10-25% only with caution and documentation (88%, level 4)

details: 🔗 RPA classes from Ward: 2-yr OS 61·9% (I, n=91), 40·0% (II, n=230), 16·8% (III, n=81)
🔗 Caudell 505-pt cohort drives the dose statement: 2-yr OS 49·3% (≥66 Gy) vs 34·2% (60·0-65·9) vs 30·4% (<60 Gy)
🔗 Vargo 2018 IMRT vs SBRT in RPA II: 2-yr OS 35·4% vs 18·6%, p<0·001; no difference when SBRT ≥35 Gy/5 fx to ≤25 cc
⚠️ 7 of 31 statements only moderate, and they cluster on the decisions that actually matter: RPA III eligibility, 66 Gy reference dose, SBRT dose, cord/brainstem limits
⚠️ Single voting round, no iterative Delphi; agreement is opinion measured against opinion, not an outcome
⚠️ Most dose-accumulation and delineation statements sit at evidence level 4 (expert consensus / extrapolation)
⚠️ Pooled toxicity across 39 studies (3766 pts): G3+ acute 32%, late 29%, carotid blowout up to 4%
⚠️ Nasopharynx and rare histologies excluded; no randomised data on sequencing reirradiation vs first-line IO
studies.significance: The operational cut is volume, not phase: ≤25 cc RPA II recurrences take IMRT or SBRT interchangeably (88%), >25 cc take IMRT (88%), and postoperative takes IMRT over SBRT (94%). Elective nodal irradiation is off at 100% agreement. Larynx/hypopharynx SBRT carries the explicit caution.
studies.monday_clinic: In a previously irradiated HNSCC recurrence being worked up for salvage, this frames selection by interval (<6mo generally off), resection status, and GTV volume, and it does not address nasopharyngeal recurrence or rare histologies.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: Expert-driven clinical practice statement from ReCOG. Core group of six radiation oncologists, three physicists and one research fellow drafted; **31 statements** went to a **single formal voting round** of **17 international radiation oncologists** (agree / disagree / no opinion, fixed 17-panellist denominator). No second round.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: Output is **agreement percentage plus an evidence level**, not an efficacy result. Thresholds prespecified: high **≥85%**, moderate **70-84%**, low **<70%**. **24 of 31 (77%)** reached high consensus; the 7 moderate statements clustered on unfavourable-prognosis subgroups, narrow therapeutic ratio, and dose prescription/fractionation.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: Definitive: **CTV = GTV + 5 mm** (94%), IMRT ~**66 Gy** for >25 cc (82%), **SBRT ~40 Gy/5 fx** for ≤25 cc (76%). Postoperative: IMRT ~**60 Gy** (94%), preferred over SBRT (94%). **Elective nodal irradiation not recommended** (100%), on Caudell's 505-pt cohort where ENI in 186 (36·8%) gave no locoregional-failure or OS gain and more acute toxicity.

analysis_sections.label: Safety
analysis_sections.body: Cumulative dose in **EQD2**, α/β 2-3 Gy for late tissues. Carotid **>120-125 Gy** raises blowout risk (94%); in a 1554-pt reirradiated cohort blowout occurred in 41 (2·6%) with 29 of 38 (76%) mortality. Mandible ORN rises above **114-119 Gy**; ORN rates 2-18% across 18 of 39 studies.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents recurrent or second primary HNSCC in a previously irradiated field considered for definitive or postoperative reirradiation. Does not represent nasopharyngeal carcinoma or rare histologies, both explicitly excluded.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: Agreement was measured once, with no opportunity for panellists to revise after seeing the distribution, so the 77% high-consensus figure is not a converged Delphi result. The dose-accumulation and delineation panels sit almost entirely at **evidence level 4**, and the authors themselves frame the thresholds as pragmatic planning objectives rather than evidence-based limits.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: Lowest agreement fell on cumulative **cord (≤50 Gy) and brainstem (≤55 Gy)** constraints, reflecting disagreement over how conservative to be and how to model tissue recovery. Sequencing reirradiation against first-line immune checkpoint inhibitors has **no randomised data**; non-randomised combination data show no unexpected safety signal to date.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: Volume and resection status, not phase of prior disease, drive technique: ≤25 cc RPA II takes IMRT or SBRT interchangeably (88%), >25 cc takes IMRT (88%), postoperative takes IMRT (94%) at ~60 Gy. Elective nodal irradiation is off at 100%, and cumulative carotid EQD2 >120-125 Gy is the hard planning ceiling.
significance_by_specialty.surgonc: Salvage surgery stays the preferred first move when feasible, and the panel extends postoperative reirradiation past strict pathology: with R0 unlikely on preoperative imaging or surgical assessment, reirradiation can be considered even without reported positive margins (82%). RPA class I (resected, >2 yr interval) with positive margins or ECE is the 100%-agreement indication.

papers.title: Stereotactic Body Radiotherapy vs Sorafenib Alone in Hepatocellular Carcinoma: The NRG Oncology/RTOG 1112 Phase 3 Randomized Clinical Trial.
papers.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Most patients with locally advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) recur within the liver following systemic therapy.

OBJECTIVE: To determine whether stereotactic body radiation therapy (SBRT) improves outcomes in patients with locally advanced HCC compared with sorafenib alone.

DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This multicenter phase 3 randomized clinical trial randomized patients with HCC 1:1 to sorafenib or SBRT followed by sorafenib, stratified by performance status, liver function, degree of metastases, and macrovascular invasion. Eligible patients had HCC unsuitable for or refractory to standard local-regional therapies and were candidates for first-line systemic therapy. Data were collected from April 2013 to March 2021, and data were analyzed from July 2022 to August 2023.

INTERVENTION: Personalized SBRT, 27.5 to 50 Gy in 5 fractions.

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary end point was overall survival (OS). Secondary end points were progression-free survival (PFS), adverse events, and quality of life.

RESULTS: Of 193 patients randomized, 177 were eligible. Accrual was stopped early due to a change in standard-of-care systemic therapy. Of 177 included patients, 150 (84.7%) were male, and the median (IQR) age was 66 (60-72) years. Macrovascular invasion was seen in 131 (74.0%). As of July 1, 2022, the median OS was 12.3 months (90% CI, 10.6-14.3) with sorafenib vs 15.8 months (90% CI, 11.4-19.2) following SBRT and sorafenib (hazard ratio [HR], 0.77; 90% CI, 0.59-1.01; 1-sided P = .06). Adjusting for stratification factors, OS was improved with SBRT (HR, 0.72; 95% CI, 0.52-0.99; 2-sided P = .04). Median PFS was improved from 5.5 months (95% CI, 3.4-6.3) with sorafenib to 9.2 months (95% CI, 7.5-11.9) with SBRT and sorafenib (HR, 0.55; 95% CI, 0.40-0.75; 2-sided P < .001). Treatment-related grade 3 or higher adverse events were seen in 37 of 88 (42%) and 39 of 83 (47%) of patients treated with sorafenib vs SBRT and sorafenib, respectively (P = .52). There were 2 treatment-related deaths in the sorafenib group (death not otherwise specified and liver failure) and 1 in the SBRT and sorafenib group (lung infection). At 6 months, improved quality of life was seen in 2 of 20 (10%) and 6 of 17 (35%) of patients treated with sorafenib and SBRT and sorafenib, respectively.

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this phase 3 randomized clinical trial, among patients with locally advanced HCC, SBRT was associated with a clinically important but not statistically significant improved overall survival compared with sorafenib alone.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT01730937.
